what: Quiz v2 draft for docs/quiz-v2.md: the two axes, the six school positions and the ten questions with their weights. A draft for Arthur to decide, not built. scripts/simulate-quiz-v2.mjs reads this file. Each option's vector is its school's direction (angle) times that school's weight in radius_by_school.

y.name: What makes it right
y.plus: who you are and what you owe

questions.prompt: Your group project is due tomorrow and one person has done almost nothing. What do you do?

options.label: Do my own part properly and stop worrying about theirs. Their effort was never mine to control.
Share out what is left in whatever way gets the group the best mark, even if I end up doing most of it.
Message them directly. Being in a group means owing the others your share, and someone has to say so.
Find out whether pushing them now would make things worse for them or for us, and only push if it would not.

questions.prompt: A friend asks what you think of an essay they are proud of. It is weak.

options.label: Tell them it is weak. A friend who only flatters is not the kind of friend I want to be.
Offer to go through it together. When one of us does badly, the rest of us have let it happen.
Say whatever is most likely to get the essay improved before it is handed in, even if that is not quite what I think.
Give my honest view once and leave it there. What they do with it is up to them.

questions.prompt: Your gran wants you at a family lunch on the day of a match you really want to play in.

options.label: Go to the lunch. Being a grandchild comes with days you turn up for, whether or not you feel like it.
Work out which choice leaves fewer people upset, me included, and do that.
Ask myself what someone I really look up to would do, and do that.
Ask the family. It is their day as much as mine, so it should be decided together.

questions.prompt: A new app shows which of your classmates are nearby and when. Your friends all use it.

options.label: Use it if it makes more people's lives easier than harder overall.
Whether I use it is my call. How everyone else uses it was never up to me.
Not unless everyone it shows has agreed. It is not only my information to give away.
Leave it if it turns friends into people who check up on each other. That is not what friends are for.

questions.prompt: You see a classmate copying in an exam.

options.label: Think about who this is going to hurt, them included, before I decide whether to say anything.
Do what an honest person would do here, even if it costs me friends.
Keep my eyes on my own paper. Their choices are theirs to answer for.
Report it if that makes the results fairer for everyone else in the year.

questions.prompt: Your younger brother keeps using your phone without asking.

options.label: Raise it with the whole family. People who live together sort things out together.
I am the older one, so I set how we treat each other's things and expect him to follow it.
Say no without making a scene. Getting angry would do more damage than a borrowed phone.
Be patient with him. I would rather be generous with my things than someone who keeps score.

questions.prompt: Your team captain keeps picking friends over better players.

options.label: Play as well as I can wherever I am put. Who gets picked is not up to me.
Push for picks based on results, because that wins the most games for all of us.
Tell the captain to their face that it is unfair. Keeping quiet would be cowardly.
Get the whole team to agree how picks should work, so nobody is left out of deciding.

questions.prompt: An AI tool could write your whole history essay, and nobody would ever know.

options.label: Write it myself. A student owes the teacher their own work, the way the teacher owes them honest marking.
Ask what using it would do to my own learning and to everyone else's marks, and if it harms either, do not use it.
Use it if the time I save does more good somewhere else than writing the essay would.
Whether anyone finds out is not the point. What I do with my own mind is the one thing that is mine.

questions.prompt: A friend tells you a secret. Passing it on would stop another friend making a big mistake.

options.label: Keep it. Being someone people can trust matters more than getting this one situation right.
Bring the two of them together. A problem between my friends belongs to all of us.
Weigh what I owe each of them. The friendship that goes back further comes first.
Pass on only as much as stops the harm, and tell the first friend that I did.

questions.prompt: Your class votes on whether an app should rank everyone's attendance where all can see it.

options.label: Vote yes if it raises attendance overall, even if a few people are embarrassed.
Vote for whatever I think is right and not worry about how the vote goes.
Vote no. It trains people to turn up for the ranking rather than because they mean to.
Vote no. A tutor should know why a student is missing, not read it off a chart.
